idiom_name: Data.define variants + case/in hash or positional patterns
implementation_notes: Data.define (Ruby 3.2) creates immutable value classes that already implement deconstruct and deconstruct_keys, so pattern matching needs no hand-written hooks: each variant is a Data class, the sum is the convention that the case lists them, and case/in destructures fields with hash patterns or positionally. Data instances compare by value and cannot be mutated, which is the closest Ruby gets to an algebraic value. Omitting else makes an unmatched value raise NoMatchingPatternError, which is the runtime stand-in for exhaustiveness.
code_sketch:
Circle = Data.define(:radius)
Square = Data.define(:side)

def area(shape)
  case shape
  in Circle(radius:) then Math::PI * radius**2
  in Square(side:)   then side**2
  end   # no else: an unknown variant raises NoMatchingPatternError
end
pitfalls: Pattern matching is duck-typed: any object answering deconstruct_keys can match a variant pattern, and a typo in the class constant silently changes which branch runs.
There is no static check that the case covers every variant; the missing-else behaviour (raise) is the only guard, and adding else silently reintroduces the gap.
Data classes are immutable but shallow - a mutable field can still be mutated, and Data.define has no keyword defaults, so every member must be supplied.

variants.name: Plain classes with deconstruct_keys + case/in (Ruby 3.0+)
variants.implementation_notes: On Ruby 3.0-3.1 pattern matching exists but the Data class does not, so each variant is an ordinary class (or Struct) that must implement deconstruct_keys itself, returning a symbol-keyed hash of the fields the patterns bind. The case/in expression then dispatches exactly as in the 3.2 form. Choose it when the runtime is pinned below 3.2 or when variants need behaviour and mutable state; otherwise Data.define removes the hook and the mutability.
variants.code_sketch:
class Circle
  attr_reader :radius
  def initialize(radius) = @radius = radius
  def deconstruct_keys(_) = { radius: radius }
end

def area(shape)
  case shape
  in Circle(radius:) then Math::PI * radius**2
  in Square(side:)   then side**2
  else raise ArgumentError, shape
  end
end
pitfalls: Forgetting deconstruct_keys makes the class match hash patterns as an empty hash, so patterns like in Circle(radius:) silently fail to bind.
Ordinary classes are mutable and identity-based for equality, so two visually identical variants are not == unless value equality is defined (or Struct/Data is used).
case/in only supports symbol keys in hash patterns, so string-keyed payloads must be converted in deconstruct_keys.
